title: Conditions Written to the Owner on Suspension for Arrears, Restoration and Restart under the Building Automation Service Plans
content:
# Conditions Written to the Owner on Suspension for Arrears, Restoration and Restart under the Building Automation Service Plans

**Suspension.** Remote access and alarm monitoring under the Building Automation Service Plans are withdrawn once an invoice stays unpaid beyond the tier's suspension period counted from the day the invoice fell due, counting calendar days with the due day excluded and the final day included. The invoice, its due day and its amount are read from the plan's own billing history; the suspension period is the tier's figure in calendar days. The final day of the period is itself within the period, and withdrawal follows once the invoice has stayed unpaid beyond it.

**While suspended.** While a plan is suspended the site's alarms are not watched and no support ticket is taken, and the desk tells the caller so rather than logging a ticket that nobody will work.

**Restoration — retired basis.** The clause "Access and monitoring are restored when the arrears are settled in full and the tier's reinstatement fee is charged" is **no longer in force** and has been superseded by the current basis on which a withdrawn plan is put back into service and charged.

**No top-up on restoration.** The support pool and alarm allowance are not topped up on reinstatement, because the plan year's credit was made once.

**Restart of a lapsed plan.** A plan that lapsed at its term end may be restarted without a fresh site survey only inside the tier's restart window counted forward in calendar days from the term end date, the end day excluded and the final day included; past that the system is surveyed again before any plan is quoted. The term end date and the plan's standing are read from the plan record.

The suspension period, the reinstatement fee and the restart window per tier are those of the tier schedule of suspension and restart figures.

## Counting illustrations (hypothetical dates)

- Suspension period of 45 days, invoice due on the 1st of March: the 2nd of March is day one and the 15th of April is day forty-five, the final day of the period. An invoice unpaid on the 15th of April has not yet stayed unpaid beyond the period; unpaid on the 16th of April it has, and remote access and alarm monitoring are withdrawn.
- Restart window of 60 days, term ended on the 30th of June: the 1st of July is day one and the 29th of August is day sixty. A restart on the 29th of August falls inside the window and needs no fresh survey; a restart sought on the 30th of August falls outside it, and the system is surveyed again before any plan is quoted.

| Handling day relative to the restart window's final day | Restart without a fresh survey |
|---|---|
| on or before the final day | yes |
| after the final day | no; the system is surveyed again first |

superseded_clauses: Access and monitoring are restored when the arrears are settled in full and the tier's reinstatement fee is charged
